items.stem: What time of day is it when the Chorus enters?
options: Sunrise
Midnight
Noon
Dusk

items.stem: Which army has just fled from Thebes?
options: The Argive army
The Athenian fleet
The Persian host
The Corinthian guard

items.stem: To what bird does the Chorus compare the invading lord of Argos?
options: An eagle
A raven
A vulture
A hawk

items.stem: Complete the Chorus's line: “O eye of golden _____”
options: night
winter
day
shadow

items.stem: To what does the Chorus compare great Ares in the battle?
options: A war-horse
A lion
A storm wind
A wolf

items.stem: How many captains attacked the city's gates?
options: Seven
Three
Twelve
Two

items.stem: What does the Chorus call for now that the war is over?
options: Feasting and dancing in the temples
A day of silent mourning for all the fallen
A new attack on Argos
The building of higher walls

items.stem: Why does the Chorus say Zeus struck the attacker?
options: Zeus hates a braggart's boast
The attacker had robbed his temple
The attacker was Zeus's old enemy
The Theban priests begged him to

items.stem: Which spring does the Chorus say the sunlight shone upon?
options: Dircè's fountain
The springs of Castaly
The river Ismenus
The sea at Aulis

items.stem: Complete the Chorus's line: “The din of _____ panic-struck they hear.”
options: Hades
Hermes
Ares
Pluto

items.stem: What colour are the shields of the invading army?
options: White
Black
Red
Gold

items.stem: What does the Chorus say each captain left behind at the gates?
options: His armour as a trophy for Zeus
His horse and chariot as a gift to the city
His sons as hostages
His spear in the city wall

items.stem: Why does the Chorus call the two brothers “that ill-starred pair”?
options: They were brothers who killed each other
They served opposite gods and died for them
They were captured by the enemy
They fled from the battle together

items.stem: What does the image of the city's “crown of towers” suggest?
options: Thebes is proud and royal, ringed with defences
Thebes has a king who wears a tower crown
Thebes is a city of temples and priests
Thebes has been burned to the ground

items.stem: How does the Chorus picture the fallen attacker before he crashes to earth?
options: As a Bacchic reveller breathing hate and flame
As a hungry wolf creeping slowly toward the gates
As a ship driven onto the rocks
As a tree cut down by an axe

items.stem: What contrast does the Chorus draw in describing the Argives' retreat?
options: They came slowly but fled faster than they came
They came at night but fled in the day
They came in ships but fled on foot
They came as friends but fled as foes

items.stem: What does “Crowned by this strange chance” suggest about how Creon became king?
options: He gained the throne through the brothers' deaths
He won the crown in an athletic contest
He was chosen by an oracle at Delphi
He took power in a revolt

items.stem: Complete the Chorus's line: “Dance and sing the live _____ long.”
options: morning
winter
night
season

items.stem: What does the Chorus imply by calling the attacker's hand impious?
options: He made war on the gods' own city and shrines
He refused to pray before the battle
He had killed a priest of Apollo
He had broken a treaty with Argos

items.stem: What is the effect of the phrase “brother slain by brother”?
options: It stresses the horror of kin killing kin
It celebrates the brothers' courage
It suggests the brothers were enemies of Zeus
It shows that the war is not over

items.stem: Which device does the Chorus use in addressing the sunbeam as an eye of golden day?
options: Apostrophe
Irony
Understatement
Hyperbole

items.stem: How does the Parodos reflect the role of the Chorus in Greek tragedy?
options: It speaks for the city and reacts to events
It acts out the whole battle on stage for the audience
It argues with the king about the war
It tells the audience how the play will end

items.stem: What view of pride does the Parodos present?
options: The gods humble those who boast
Pride is the source of a city's strength
Pride belongs only to kings and heroes
Pride is forgiven when a war is won

items.stem: What does the Chorus mean by “Forced by the Dragon”?
options: Driven back by the might of Thebes
Chased by a real monster
Burned by a fire-breathing beast
Frightened by an evil sign in the sky

items.stem: Complete the Chorus's line: “Bacchus, shaker of the _____!”
options: heavens
ground
ocean
market

items.stem: Why does the Chorus say the attacker came “Outbreathing hate and flame”?
options: To show his violent, destructive fury
To show that he was really a god in disguise
To show he was sick with fever
To show he was singing a hymn

items.stem: Which theme of the play is first suggested by the Parodos's account of the brothers?
options: Family bonds turned to deadly conflict
Love that overcomes all enemies and every hatred
The wisdom of old age
The power of money to corrupt

items.stem: How does the Parodos's form differ from the Prologue's?
options: It is a sung choral ode rather than spoken dialogue
It is spoken by a single actor alone
It is written in prose
It has no rhythm or rhyme at all

items.stem: What is ironic about the Chorus's call to blot out memories of war?
options: The war's dead will soon cause new conflict
The elders have not seen a war in many years
The city has actually lost the war
The god of war is their patron
